judged_text: In updateEvent, when externalCalendarId is falsy the fallback event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId compares stored externalIds against the falsy value and can never match, so selectedCalendar is always undefined (the old code used the destination row's externalId). Reschedules of bookings whose calendar reference lacks externalCalendarId (legacy references, the other_calendar path that passes null, and new references produced by the no-credentialId creation branch that never sets result.externalId) now call Google events.update with calendarId undefined, which fails, so the calendar event silently stops being updated on reschedule.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent`, the fallback branch `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is logically wrong when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (null/undefined), because it compares every `cal.externalId` against that falsy value and will not select the intended destination calendar. Previously (when `destinationCalendar` was a single object) the fallback was `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`, which would work for legacy references lacking `externalCalendarId`. The diff also shows multiple call sites now pass `externalCalendarId` as `null` when missing (e.g. `EventManager.updateCalendarEvents` builds `calenderExternalId: string | null = null` and passes it into `updateEvent`), making this broken branch reachable and likely causing updates to target the wrong calendar (or no calendar) for reschedules/updates when `externalCalendarId` is absent.
